lead_text:
I've set up the tools and started the design record. Before the INTENT stage I need some answers from you. The design files only allow facts you state, so I haven't assumed anything below.

**Done so far (GROUND stage)**
- The tool check passed: FreeCAD, CadQuery, build123d, the viewer and the renderer are all in place. A background warm-up is running.
- I created the design record from the template and filled it in from your brief. The record checker passes on it (`validate.py`: ok).
- I wrote five requirements: strength under 200 N + 15 N, tip deflection under 2 mm, the rail mounting, the shelf screws, and 6061-T6 CNC from a bureau ×20.

**First numbers, for context (rough hand estimates, not checked results)**
- The bending moment at the wall is about 200 N × 250 mm + 15 N × ~125 mm ≈ 52 N·m.
- If the bracket pivots on its bottom edge, the top M6 screw pulls out at roughly 0.6–0.7 kN. The rivet-nut rating therefore matters for safety.
- The 2 mm deflection limit will probably decide the section size more than strength does. The material data I have for 6061-T6 has no stiffness (Young's modulus) value, so I'll need a sourced figure later.

**Questions** (short answers are fine; "accept" takes the suggestion in brackets)

| # | Question |
|---|---|
| Q-001 | Are these 20 brackets finished parts for real use, or a prototype first? [finished parts] |
| Q-003 | Operating temperature range, and any heat sources nearby? [10–35 °C, none] |
| Q-004 | Any oils, coolants or solvents near the shelving? Is the rail painted, galvanised or bare? Bracket finish: bare, bead-blasted or clear anodised? (Aluminium touching steel can corrode, which is why I ask.) [no chemicals; clear anodised] |
| Q-005 | Is the 200 N sustained (stored items), occasional, or can it come with impact? Any sideways or upward loads? Is the 200 N per bracket? [sustained, per bracket, no impact] |
| Q-006 | Design life in years, and roughly how often the shelf is loaded and unloaded? [10 years, light use] |
| Q-007 | Any looks or finish needs (visible faces, rounded edges)? [break sharp edges, no other looks requirement] |
| Q-008 | What happens if it fails: do people work under the shelf? Any standards or house rules? Who approves the design? |
| Q-009 | Budget per bracket or for the batch, and lead time? |
| Q-010 | Which CNC bureau? Can you share its smallest inside corner radius, the tolerances it can hold, whether it cuts from plate or bar, and whether it supplies a 3.1 material certificate? Does it also do the finishing? |
| Q-011 | What must the release be backed by: analysis only (hand calculation + FEA), or will you also load-test a first bracket, e.g. at 300 N? |
| Q-012 | Fitting order: bracket onto the rail first, then the shelf screwed on from below? Hex key used from the front? [yes] |
| Q-013 | General tolerance for the drawings? [ISO 2768-mK] |
| Q-014 | Rivet nuts: make, steel or aluminium, rated pull-out force and maximum torque? Does the rail stand off the wall (a channel) or lie flat on it? Must the bracket's back plate stay within the 40 mm rail face? |
| Q-015 | Cap screws: strength class, finish and length (8.8 zinc or A2-70 stainless)? Wood screws: head, drive type and material? |
| Q-016 | What safety factor on yield must the bracket keep under the 215 N case? [2.0] |

**Two setup questions**
- **Results in git:** should generated results (STEP, GLB, renders, check results) be stored in git, with Git LFS for STEP and GLB? Or kept out of git? I need this answer before the first build.
- **Documentation depth:** the record is set to `pro` (between `maker` and `regulated`). Keep that?

Once you answer, I'll record the answers and move on to INTENT, where I compare the full design and manufacturing options and ask for your approval. Then come the concept variants, the VARIANT gate and the L1 LAYOUT with its freeze gate. Nothing moves forward until you reply.
reply:
Answers from the user:
- Production: end-use brackets for our own workshop, not a prototype.
- Indoor, dry workshop, 10 to 35 °C. No chemicals, UV or corrosion exposure.
- As machined and deburred, no coating. The two M6 holes must be at 32 mm pitch within ±0.2 mm to meet the rail's rivet nuts.
- Static 200 N downward at the shelf's front edge, 250 mm from the wall face, plus about 15 N shelf weight per bracket. Boxes are placed, not dropped; no impact, vibration or cyclic rating. Use a safety factor of 2 on yield for the 200 N case. Tip deflection under 200 N below 2 mm.
- No motion; it is a static bracket.
- If it fails the shelf falls; nobody stands under it. No regulatory standard applies. I approve the design myself.
- 20 brackets, about 15 EUR each from the bureau, within three weeks.
- No in-house machining. An outsourced CNC bureau mills 3-axis from 6061-T6 plate up to 20 mm thick; its published general capability is ±0.1 mm and minimum internal corner radius 1 mm. We have no calibration records for it. The fasteners are bought.
- 6061-T6 aluminium for the bracket; the screws are standard steel catalogue parts.
- The rail face is 40 mm wide and 2 mm steel, with M6 rivet nuts at 32 mm vertical pitch. The bracket's back face sits on the rail face and two ISO 4762 M6 screws go into the rivet nuts.
- 18 mm plywood, 250 mm deep, resting on the bracket's top flange. Two 4 × 16 mm countersunk wood screws go up through the flange into the board.
- Do not store generated results in git: set storage.results_in_git to false.
- I select the variant you recommend. VARIANT gate approved.
- I have no further information on that. Use your recommended option, record it as a bounded assumption in a decision record, and continue.

lead_text:
The v2 layout passed every fast check and the full check. The provisional gate is recorded as DR-007. The LAYOUT freeze is now waiting for your approval, and I've stopped there as scoped.

**One failure along the way.** The first full check, on v1, failed: both wood-screw models sat 0.141 mm off their countersinks, so the check flagged them as not connected to the bracket. I voided that provisional gate (DR-006), seated the screws properly and built v2.

## What was decided before the layout
- **Your answers and my assumptions (DR-001):** the use case is confirmed from your answers. Where you had no information, I used my recommended option and recorded it as an open assumption (ASM-001 to ASM-010).
- **Results not in git (DR-002):** `storage.results_in_git: false`, and the git ignore rules are written.
- **Route (DR-003):** 6061-T6 plate, 3-axis CNC at the bureau, catalogue screws. It stays "conditional" until strength and stiffness are analysed later. Laser-cut bent steel and a bought steel bracket were ruled out because they don't meet your material and process requirement.
- **Concept (DR-004):** you pre-approved my pick. I recommended B, the tapered cantilever:
  - It has clear tool access to both screw types.
  - It is the simplest shape to machine.
  - It is deepest where the bending load is highest.
  - The other two were A (open truss) and C (solid gusset).

## Layout v2

| Part | Description | Make/buy | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|
| WB-0001 | Bracket. 18 mm side profile from 20 mm plate, 250 mm arm, beam 40 mm deep at the wall tapering to 14 mm at the tip, 12 × 120 mm back leg. About 373 g. | make (CNC bureau) | 1 |
| WB-0002 | ISO 4762 M6×20, class 8.8, zinc plated (ASM-004) | buy | 2 |
| WB-0003 | 4×16 countersunk wood screw, 90° head, zinc plated (ASM-004) | buy | 2 |

**Rail mounting (IF-001):**
- Two 6.6 mm holes at z −60 and −92 mm, measured pitch 32.000 mm (±0.2 mm goes on the drawing later).
- A 14 × 1.7 mm recess around each hole on the back face clears the rivet-nut flange (ASM-003).
- The bracket is 18 mm wide, inside the 40 mm rail face.

**Shelf fixing (IF-002):**
- Two 4.5 mm holes at x 190 and 235 mm, with 90° countersinks under a 5 mm flange.
- Each screw goes 11.2 mm into the 18 mm board.

**Fitting order:**
1. Fit the M6 screws through the back leg into the rivet nuts with a 5 mm hex key from the front.
2. Lay the shelf on the bracket and drive the wood screws upward from below.

In the CAD, the hex-key path and the screwdriver path below each screw are clear of the bracket: measured overlap 0.0 mm³, with a check that the measurement method does detect overlap.

## Checks on v2

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Record validation | passed, 0 findings |
| Changed-parts check | passed (6 pairs) |
| **Full check, all 10 pairs** | **passed**, every part touching its neighbour, no interference |
| Renders (5 views) | passed |
| Parts list | 1 bracket, 2 cap screws, 2 wood screws |
| Layout evidence gate | passed: CAD evidence for hole pitch, rail mounting and shelf fixing (EV-005 to EV-008) |
| Joint sweep / motion render | not applicable: no moving joints, so no untested gaps between sample poses |

**Not yet shown:** strength and deflection need the later analysis stage. My rough hand estimate is about 10 MPa at the bracket root against the 120 MPa limit, but that is not evidence. The bureau's ±0.1 mm is published, not measured, and the wood-screw grade is still unknown.

**Not committed yet:** these v2 changes are staged but not in git. The commit check requires the check stamp's stage to match `flow.stage`, which reads `parts` after the provisional gate. I'll commit once the gate is decided.

lead_text:
I recorded the LAYOUT freeze approval, but I could not commit: the commit check refuses it.

**Recorded**
- **DR-008:** your acceptance of unproved between-sample intervals. v2 has no moving joints, so no sweep ran and no intervals were reported. The acceptance covers an empty set and does not carry over to later versions.
- **DR-009:** LAYOUT freeze approved on v2, citing DR-007 (provisional gate) and DR-008. `flow.recheck_from` is `layout`. DR-009 also lists what is still open:
  - ASM-006, ASM-009 and ASM-010 were not separately confirmed and stay open, along with the other assumptions.
  - The CNC 6061-T6 route stays conditional until strength and stiffness are analysed.
- The design log has the gate entry. The record checker passes with 0 findings.

**Why the commit is blocked**
- The provisional gate (DR-007) moved `flow.stage` to `parts`, as the flow requires.
- A commit is allowed only when the check stamp is for the current stage. The parts-stage check fails because no parts-stage evidence exists yet (purchased-part identities and ratings, CNC feature and stock checks).
- `stamp.py --verify` exits 2, which means do not commit. I didn't bypass it, and I didn't move `flow.stage` back to `layout`, because that would contradict DR-007.
- Every `hw/` change since the last commit (layout v2, evidence, DR-005 to DR-009) is staged but not committed. The last commit is the concept stage (DR-004).

**Decision for you:**
- **Commit now with `flow.stage: layout`.** The stamp passes at layout, but the record would no longer match the provisional gate's stage change.
- **Commit at the end of L2.** The record keeps its true state, but nothing from this session is in git until then.

I've stopped here and not started L2.
